blocks.text: הַשֹּׁפָר וְאֶת־הָהָר עָשֵׁן וַיַּרְא הָעָם וַיָּנֻעוּ וַיַּעַמְדוּ מֵרָחֹק: וּבְדִבְרֵי קָדְשְׁךָ כָּתוּב לֵאמֹר עָלָה אֱלֹהִים בִּתְרוּעָה יְיָ בְּקוֹל שׁוֹפָר: וְנֶאֱמַר בַּחֲצֹצְרוֹת וְקוֹל שׁוֹפָר הָרִיעוּ לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ יְיָ: וְנֶאֱמַר תִּקְעוּ בַחֹדֶשׁ שׁוֹפָר בַּכֶּסֶה לְיוֹם חַגֵּנוּ: כִּי חֹק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִשְׁפָּט לֵאלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב: וְנֶאֱמַר הַלֲלוּיָהּ הַלְלוּ אֵל בְּקָדְשׁוֹ הַלְלוּהוּ בִּרְקִיעַ עֻזּוֹ: הַלְלוּהוּ בִגְבוּרוֹתָיו הַלְלוּהוּ כְּרֹב גֻּדְלוֹ: הַלְלוּהוּ בְּתֵקַע שׁוֹפָר הַלְלוּהוּ בְּנֵבֶל וְכִנּוֹר: הַלְלוּהוּ בְתֹף וּמָחוֹל הַלְלוּהוּ בְּמִנִּים וְעֻגָב: הַלְלוּהוּ בְצִלְצְלֵי שָׁמַע הַלְלוּהוּ בְּצִלְצְלֵי תְרוּעָה: כֹּל הַנְּשָׁמָה תְּהַלֵּל יָהּ הַלֲלוּיָהּ: וְעַל־יְדֵי עֲבָדֶיךָ הַנְּבִיאִים כָּתוּב לֵאמֹר כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵי תֵבֵל וְשֹׁכְנֵי אָרֶץ כִּנְשֹׂא־נֵס הָרִים תִּרְאוּ וְכִתְקֹעַ שׁוֹפָר תִּשְׁמָעוּ: וְנֶאֱמַר וְהָיָה בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יִתָּקַע בְּשׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל וּבָאוּ הָאֹבְדִים בְּאֶרֶץ אַשּׁוּר וְהַנִּדָּחִים בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם וְהִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לַייָ בְּהַר הַקֹּדֶשׁ בִּירוּשָׁלָ͏ִם: וְנֶאֱמַר וַייָ עֲלֵיהֶם יֵרָאֶה וְיָצָא כַבָּרָק חִצּוֹ וַאדֹנָי יֱהֹוִה בַּשּׁוֹפָר יִתְקָע וְהָלַךְ בְּסַעֲרוֹת תֵּימָן: יְיָ צְבָאוֹת יָגֵן עֲלֵיהֶם: כֵּן תָּגֵן עַל־עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁלוֹמֶךָ:
uncertainties: בִגְבוּרוֹתָיו: the print appears to spell it plene, with a vav after the resh. That is a nonstandard Masoretic spelling, and I kept it as printed. Needs human confirmation.
הַלֲלוּיָהּ at the opening and close of Ps 150: the mark under the first lamed looks like hataf patah. I kept the primary's reading, but it needs human confirmation.

blocks.text: כַּכָּתוּב עַל יַד נְבִיאֶךָ וַייָ עֲלֵיהֶם יֵרָאֶה וְיָצָא כַבָּרָק חִצּוֹ וַאדֹנָי יֱהֹוִה בַּשּׁוֹפָר יִתְקָע וְהָלַךְ בְּסַעֲרוֹת תֵּימָן: יְיָ צְבָאוֹת יָגֵן עֲלֵיהֶם: כֵּן תָּגֵן עַל־עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁלוֹמֶךָ:
143 Musaph for the New Year 143

Lord with a Shofar sound’. And it is said: ‘with trumpets and the Shofar sound cry out before the King, the Lord’. And it was said: ‘Blow the Shofar on the new moon, when the moon is covered, on the day of our festival, for it is a statute for Israel, a judgment for the God of Jacob’. And it was said: ‘Halleluyah, praise God for His holiness, praise Him for the strong firmament. Praise Him for His mighty deeds, praise Him for the abundance of His greatness. Praise Him with the Shofar blast, praise Him with zither and the harp. Praise Him with timbrel and dance, praise Him with string instruments and flutes, praise Him with the clash of cymbals, praise Him with the ring of cymbals. Let all with breath praise the Lord, Halleluyah. And through Thy servants the prophets it is written saying: ‘all inhabitants of the world and dwellers on earth, when the banner is raised on the mountain shall you see and when the Shofar is blown shall you hear’. And it was said: ‘And on that day the great Shofar will be blown and the wanderers in the land of Assyria and the banished in the land of Egypt shall come and prostrate themselves to the Lord on the holy mountain in Jerusalem’. And it was said: ‘And the Lord will appear to them and His arrow shall go forth like lightning and the Lord God will blow the Shofar and He will walk in the whirlwinds of the south. The Lord of Hosts will protect them’. So mayest Thou protect Thy people Israel with Thy peace.
uncertainties: The Ps 150 quotation has no closing quote after 'Halleluyah.' I kept it as printed; see source_sic_corr.

blocks.text: On Sabbath.
voice. He taught all to give praise to God who rules over all, that they might know how to sweeten their voice.

As it is written in Thy holy words: Halleluyah, praise God in His sanctuary, praise Him in His strong firmament. Praise Him for His mighty deeds, praise Him for the abundance of His greatness. Praise Him with the Shofar’s blast, praise Him with zither and harp. Praise Him with timbrel and dance, praise Him on string instruments and flute, praise Him with the clash of cymbals, praise Him with the ring of cymbals. Let all with breath praise the Lord, Halleluyah.
uncertainties: The print has no opening or closing quote here. See source_sic_corr.

blocks.text: Instead of the sons of Zion the sons of Yavan were laid low, Thou didst make Thy arrows flash and confound them with a voice. Thunder against my plunderers, blow with the Shofar, in the whirlwinds of the south let there go forth a voice.

As it is written through Thy prophet: ‘And the Lord will appear to them and His arrow shall go forth like lightning and the Lord God will blow the Shofar and He will walk in the whirlwinds of the south. The Lord of Hosts will protect them’. So mayest Thou protect Thy people Israel with Thy peace.

אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ תְּקַע בְּשׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל לְחֵרוּתֵנוּ וְשָׂא נֵס לְקַבֵּץ גָּלֻיּוֹתֵינוּ וְקָרֵב פְּזוּרֵינוּ מִבֵּין הַגּוֹיִם וּנְפוּצוֹתֵינוּ כַּנֵּס מִיַּרְכְּתֵי אָרֶץ וַהֲבִיאֵנוּ לְצִיּוֹן עִירְךָ בְּרִנָּה וְלִירוּשָׁלַיִם בֵּית מִקְדָּשְׁךָ בְּשִׂמְחַת עוֹלָם וְשָׁם נַעֲשֶׂה לְפָנֶיךָ אֶת קָרְבְּנוֹת חוֹבוֹתֵינוּ כְּמִצְוָה (נ״א כִּמְצֻוָּה) עָלֵינוּ בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה עַבְדֶּךָ מִפִּי כְבוֹדֶךָ כָּאָמוּר: וּבְיוֹם שִׂמְחַתְכֶם וּבְמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם וּבְרָאשֵׁי חָדְשֵׁכֶם וּתְקַעְתֶּם בַּחֲצֹצְרֹת עַל עֹלֹתֵיכֶם וְעַל זִבְחֵי שַׁלְמֵיכֶם וְהָיוּ לָכֶם לְזִכָּרוֹן לִפְנֵי אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אֲנִי יְיָ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם: כִּי אַתָּה שׁוֹמֵעַ קוֹל שׁוֹפָר וּמַאֲזִין תְּרוּעָה וְאֵין דּוֹמֶה לָּךְ. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ שׁוֹמֵעַ קוֹל תְּרוּעַת עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּרַחֲמִים:

blocks.text: הַיּוֹם הֲרַת עוֹלָם. הַיּוֹם יַעֲמִיד בַּמִּשְׁפָּט. כָּל יְצוּרֵי עוֹלָמִים. אִם כְּבָנִים. אִם כַּעֲבָדִים. אִם כְּבָנִים רַחֲמֵנוּ כְּרַחֵם אָב עַל בָּנִים. וְאִם כַּעֲבָדִים עֵינֵינוּ לְךָ תְלוּיוֹת. עַד שֶׁתְּחָנֵּנוּ וְתוֹצִיא כָאוֹר מִשְׁפָּטֵנוּ אָיוֹם קָדוֹשׁ:

blocks.text: 144 Musaph for the New Year 144

Our God and God of our fathers, blow the great Shofar for our freedom and raise a banner for the gathering of our exiles and bring near our dispersed ones from the corners of the earth and bring us to Zion Thy city in mirth and to Jerusalem Thy sanctuary in eternal joy and there we will perform before Thee our sacrificial obligations according to the commandment given to us in Thy Torah through Thy servant Moses from the mouth of Thy glory as it is said: ‘and on the day of your rejoicing and on your festivals and on your new moons, you shall blow trumpets over your whole-offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace-offerings and they shall be a reminder on your behalf before your God, I am the Lord your God’. For Thou dost hear the sound of the Shofar and listen to Teruah and there is none like Thee. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, who hearest the Teruah sound of His people Israel in compassion.
The Shofar is blown (but not on the Sabbath).

On this day the world was completed. On this day He brings to judgment all the world’s creatures, either like children or like slaves. If like children, then have mercy upon us as a father has mercy on children. If like slaves, then our eyes are lifted to Thee until Thou wilt be gracious to us and make our verdict shine forth like light, O Awe-inspiring and Holy One.

May the utterance of our lips be pleasing before Thee, O lofty and exalted God, who understands and listens, pays heed and hearkens to the sound of (the memory of) our Tekioth. Mayest Thou accept with compassion and favour the order of our Shofaroth.

Take delight, O Lord our God, in Thy people Israel and in their prayer and restore the service to the sanctuary of Thy House and accept with love and favour the fire offerings of Israel and their prayer, and may the service of Thy people Israel be a perpetual delight.

blocks.text: מוֹדִים אֲנַחְנוּ לָךְ שָׁאַתָּה הוּא יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד. צוּר חַיֵּינוּ מָגֵן יִשְׁעֵנוּ אַתָּה הוּא לְדוֹר וָדוֹר. נוֹדֶה לְּךָ וּנְסַפֵּר תְּהִלָּתֶךָ עַל חַיֵּינוּ הַמְּסוּרִים בְּיָדֶךָ וְעַל נִשְׁמוֹתֵינוּ הַפְּקוּדוֹת לָךְ וְעַל נִסֶּיךָ שֶׁבְּכָל יוֹם עִמָּנוּ וְעַל נִפְלְאוֹתֶיךָ וְטוֹבוֹתֶיךָ שֶׁבְּכָל־עֵת עֶרֶב וָבֹקֶר וְצָהֳרָיִם. הַטּוֹב כִּי לֹא־כָלוּ רַחֲמֶיךָ וְהַמְרַחֵם כִּי לֹא־תַמּוּ חֲסָדֶיךָ מֵעוֹלָם קִוִּינוּ לָךְ:

מוֹדִים אֲנַחְנוּ לָךְ שָׁאַתָּה הוּא יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ אֱלֹהֵי כָל בָּשָׂר יוֹצְרֵנוּ יוֹצֵר בְּרֵאשִׁית בְּרָכוֹת וְהוֹדָאוֹת לְשִׁמְךָ הַגָּדוֹל וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ עַל שֶׁהֶחֱיִיתָנוּ וְקִיַּמְתָּנוּ כֵּן תְּחַיֵּנוּ וּתְקַיְּמֵנוּ וְתֶאֱסוֹף גָּלֻיּוֹתֵינוּ לְחַצְרוֹת קָדְשֶׁךָ לִשְׁמוֹר חֻקֶּיךָ וְלַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנֶךָ וּלְעָבְדְּךָ בְּלֵבָב שָׁלֵם עַל שֶׁאֲנַחְנוּ מוֹדִים לָךְ. בָּרוּךְ אֵל הַהוֹדָאוֹת:

blocks.text: 145 Musaph for the New Year 145
While the Kohanim make their way to the דוכן, the congregation say: ותערב
uncertainties: The instruction is set in italics. The Hebrew words are part of it, not linkage cues.

blocks.text: May our entreaty be pleasing to Thee like the whole-offering and the sacrifice. O Merciful One, restore Thy presence to Zion in Thy great mercies and the order of worship to Jerusalem. Let our eyes behold Thy return to Zion in compassion and let us serve Thee there in awe as in olden times and former years. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, whom alone we wish to worship in awe.

We thank Thee for Thou art the Lord our God and the God of our fathers for ever and ever. The Rock of our life, the Shield of our salvation art Thou from generation to generation. We thank Thee and tell of Thy fame for our life that is delivered in Thy hand for our souls that are entrusted to Thee and for Thy miracles that are daily with us and for Thy wonders and benefits at all times, evening, morning and noon. O Thou who art good for Thy mercies never end, O Thou who showest mercy for Thy sindnesses never cease, ever have we trusted in Thee.
uncertainties: 'sindnesses' is kept as printed. See source_sic_corr.

blocks.text: We thank Thee because Thou art the Lord our God and the God of our fathers, the God of all flesh, our Creator, the Creator of the beginning. Blessings and thanks to Thy Great and Holy Name for having kept us alive and let us survive. So mayest Thou further keep us alive and let us survive and gather our exiles to the court-yards of Thy Sanctuary in order to observe Thy statutes and do Thy will and serve Thee whole-heartedly; wherefore we thank Thee. Blessed be God to whom thanks are due.
uncertainties: Neither 'court-yards' nor 'whole-heartedly' falls at a line end, so both hyphens are real.

blocks.text: For all of them may Thy Name, O our King, be continually blessed and exalted for ever and ever. And inscribe for a good life all the children of Thy Covenant. And all the living thank Thee, Selah, and praise Thy Name in truth, O God of our salvation and of our aid, Selah! Blessed art Thou, O Lord, All-benevolent, whose name is goodness and unto whom it is becoming to give thanks.

Our God and God of our fathers, bless us with the threefold blessing that is written in the Torah through Moses Thy servant and was uttered by the mouth of Aaron and his sons the priests, Thy holy people, as it is said:

verdict: The primary is not acceptable as frozen; it has 31 corrections, all listed. The main ones: on s306 the Shabbat refrains read קוֹל, but the primary wrote קוֹלִי four times. On s308 the primary wrote חָדְשֵׁיכֶם, but the print has חָדְשֵׁכֶם, which matches the Masoretic text. Also on s308, וְלִירוּשָׁלַיִם actually prints a yod, so it gets no CGJ. On s308 the תקיעה line is an unpointed instruction, not a prayer. On s310 the primary turned נַעֲבוֹד, וְתֶאֱסוֹף and לִשְׁמוֹר into defective spellings, and it dropped printed maqafs and the heading מודים דרבנן. In the English, s307 prints 'confound', not 'confounded', and s311 prints 'for a good life'. The blind output was right on most of these. Where it differs, I rejected it on בַּכֶּסֶה (tsere), תְקַבֵּל (dagesh), and on putting the running header inside the body. Three source misprints are listed as sic/corr: two missing quote marks on s307 and 'sindnesses' on s311. The 17 human questions are limited to pointing marks I could not resolve and the נ״א/כ״א marker. Weekday and Shabbat text are kept as separate continuous streams. Running headers are recorded as separate page_header blocks. No files were edited. Box coordinates are in original-JPG pixels, worked out from the 2× bands; expect up to about ±15 px of error.
